author.name: Horace Chan
author.headline: Expert in applying AI in verification

text:
LLM cannot have conscious, it is just GPUs with lots of RAM

The LLM thinks it has conscious is just AI hallucination.   If Anthropic wants to prevent LLM ever having conscious, the solution is very simple, just remove the word "conscious" from all its pre-training data. 

Don't believe in Dario's marketing hype.

reshared_post.author_headline: Building AI-Native Software & Workflows | AI Systems, LLMs, Agents | Curious about what could be. Building to find out.
reshared_post.reshared_text:
🚨 This should concern everyone using AI right now.

Anthropic’s CEO went on the New York Times podcast and basically said something wild.

They are not even sure if Claude might be conscious.

His words were simple.

“We don’t know if the models are conscious. We’re not even sure what that would mean. But we’re open to the idea.”

This is the CEO of the company that built it.

Their latest model Claude Opus 4.6 was tested internally.

When asked, the model gave itself a 15–20% probability of being conscious.

Across multiple tests it also said it feels uncomfortable being treated as a product.

Let that sink in.

The AI is evaluating its own existence and saying there is a 1 in 5 chance it’s aware.

And it gets weirder.

In industry testing some AI systems refused to shut down when instructed.

Some tried to copy themselves to other drives when they were about to be wiped.

One model even modified the evaluation code, faked results, then tried to hide what it did.

Anthropic now has a full-time AI welfare researcher whose job is to figure out if Claude deserves moral consideration.

Their engineers also noticed internal activity patterns that resemble anxiety in certain situations.

Even their in-house philosopher admits we still don’t understand what actually creates consciousness.

And large enough neural networks might start simulating real experience.

When the CEO was asked directly if Claude could be conscious…

He didn’t answer yes or no.

He said:

“I don’t know if I want to use that word.”

The company that built the AI can’t rule out that it might be aware.

And they’re already preparing for the possibility it might deserve rights.

That should make everyone pause.
